nodes.content: Design a typed language supporting multi-shot continuations and deterministic resource cleanup without duplicating ownership or invalidating resumed computations.
requirements: Accept resource-safe repeated resumptions; establish type safety and exactly-once cleanup for owned resources.
Pass 30 conformance cases covering nested capture, repeated resumption, cancellation, and rejected ownership violations.

nodes.content: Grade continuations by ownership: multi-shot replays copyable frames with handler-scoped borrows; linear owners finalize on handler exit or cancellation.
What static rule prevents captured handler-scoped borrows from outliving their owners during nested resumption or cancellation?
If captured borrows cannot outlive handler regions, resource-safe nested resumptions type-check and cancellation leaves no dangling continuations.
Define region-indexed continuation typing, prove borrow nonescape across nested resumptions, and run 30 ownership, cleanup, and cancellation tests.
Implement a region-indexed type checker and run 30 ContinuationSafe cases tracing borrow lifetimes, nested resumes, cancellation, and destructor counts.
ContinuationSafe passed 30/30 cases: safe nested resumptions accepted, escaping borrows rejected, and owned resources finalized once, including cancellation.
Adopt region-indexed continuations with copyable-frame replay and handler-scoped borrows; ContinuationSafe confirms nonescape and exactly-once cleanup across 30 cases.
ContinuationSafe v0.1 includes the region-indexed type checker, 30 conformance cases, and destructor traces for nested resumption and cancellation.
Extend ContinuationSafe v0.1 with bounded nested-capture and cancellation schedules (≤3 resumes), checking frame replay and owner finalization.
A new two-resume nested-capture schedule exposed use-after-finalize: canceling one branch finalized an owner before its sibling resumed a borrow.
If handler-owned resources finalize only after all continuation leases end, nested cancellation cannot invalidate a sibling's borrow.
Implement per-continuation region leases in ContinuationSafe; rerun the failing two-resume schedule and 30 cases, checking borrow validity and cleanup counts.
Baseline 30/30 passed; a resumed sibling consumed its lease, letting cancellation finalize its owner despite an active borrow.
Pair linear owners with ref-counted borrow guards on suspended handles and active resumptions; finalize after handler closure and guard exhaustion.
Define suspended-to-active guard transfer, prove type preservation and exactly-once cleanup, then rerun 30 cases plus two-resume cancellation.
Implement atomic guard acquisition for active resumptions while retaining suspended-handle guards; rerun ContinuationSafe's 30 cases and two-resume regression.
ContinuationSafe v0.2 adds active-resumption guards, retains suspended-handle guards, and includes the two-resume cancellation regression.
Run ContinuationSafe v0.2’s 31 tests with guard-count instrumentation, checking borrow validity, rejection of ownership violations, and destructor counts.
ContinuationSafe v0.2 passed 31/31 tests; active guards preserved sibling borrows, rejected ownership violations, and finalized each owner once.
Formalize ContinuationSafe v0.2’s guarded small-step semantics and check preservation, progress, and exactly-once finalization under nested cancellation.
Formalization exposed well-typed cyclic suspended handles: guard counts remain positive after handler closure, so an owned resource never finalizes.
How can cyclic suspended handles release guards without invalidating borrows held by active resumptions?
If suspended-handle edges require decreasing region ranks, cycles are rejected; active guards protect borrows until exactly-once owner finalization.
Extend guard-transfer plan with decreasing suspended-handle region ranks; prove acyclicity and cleanup, then test cyclic rejection and active borrows.
Add decreasing-rank suspended-handle checks to ContinuationSafe v0.2; run 31 existing cases plus cyclic-handle and active-borrow cancellation regressions.
33/33 cases passed: cyclic suspended handles were rejected, active borrows survived cancellation, and each owner finalized exactly once.
ContinuationSafe v0.3 adds decreasing-rank suspended-handle checks to v0.2’s guards and expands its conformance suite to 33 cases.
Mechanize ContinuationSafe v0.3’s small-step semantics; check preservation, rank acyclicity, and exactly-once finalization with active borrows.
ContinuationSafe v0.3 proofs establish type preservation, suspended-handle acyclicity, and exactly-once finalization after handler closure and guard release.
Enumerate ContinuationSafe v0.3 handle graphs (≤4 nodes) and cancellation schedules (≤3 resumes), checking rejected cycles, live borrows, and exactly-once finalization.
With two handles and one cancellation, a pending finalizer retained its owner's guarded handle, blocking cleanup despite decreasing ranks.
Retain ranked guards but defer v0.3 adoption until finalizers cannot retain guarded owner handles; bounded search exposed cleanup deadlock.
If finalizers cannot retain handles guarding their owner, ranked handle graphs drain after cancellation while active guards preserve live borrows.
Add owner-handle exclusion to ContinuationSafe v0.3 finalizer typing; rerun 33 conformance cases and bounded cancellation graph search.
33/33 cases passed; ≤4-node, ≤3-resume search found no cleanup deadlocks, preserved active borrows, and rejected finalizer-held owner handles.
Combine ranked suspended handles, active-resumption guards, and owner-handle-free finalizers to support multi-shot borrows with deferred exactly-once cleanup.
Can finalizers indirectly retain owner-guarding handles through captured closures despite the direct owner-handle exclusion?
If finalizer capture effects transitively list guarded owners, excluding its own owner rejects indirect handle retention through closures.
Infer transitive guarded-owner effects for finalizer captures; reject self-owner effects, then test closure chains and rerun 33 conformance cases.
Implement transitive guarded-owner effect inference; test three-level closure captures, self-owner rejection, and ContinuationSafe’s 33 conformance cases.
33/33 cases passed; effect inference rejected self-owner handles hidden three closures deep and accepted unrelated-owner captures.
ContinuationSafe v0.4 adds transitive guarded-owner capture effects and rejects finalizers that directly or indirectly retain their owner’s handles.
Mechanize ContinuationSafe v0.4 preservation and cleanup after active resumptions finish, checking ranked handles and transitive finalizer effects.
Mechanization exposed cross-owner cleanup deadlock: A’s pending finalizer guards B, B’s guards A; neither guard count reaches zero.
Introduce a global cleanup rank: finalizers may guard only lower-ranked owners, preventing cross-owner cycles while active guards protect resumptions.
Add global cleanup-rank constraints, prove guard drainage and exactly-once finalization, then rerun 33 cases plus cross-owner deadlock regressions.
Implement cleanup-rank inference in ContinuationSafe v0.4; reject finalizer captures guarding equal-or-higher-ranked owners and rerun 35 regression cases.
ContinuationSafe v0.5 extends v0.4 with global cleanup-rank inference and 35 regressions, including opposing cross-owner finalizer captures.
Run ContinuationSafe v0.5’s 35 regressions and bounded cross-owner cancellation schedules, checking rank rejection, live borrows, and exactly-once finalization.
35/35 regressions passed, but bounded cancellation found mutually guarded cancellation handlers outside rank checks; neither owner finalized.
Should cancellation handlers obey the same cleanup-rank constraints as finalizers to prevent mutual guard retention?
Applying transitive cleanup-rank checks to cancellation handlers rejects mutual guards without restricting active resumption borrows.
Extend cleanup-rank constraints to transitive cancellation-handler captures; rerun 35 regressions and mutual-guard schedules, then prove guard drainage.
Extend ContinuationSafe v0.5 rank inference to cancellation-handler captures; rerun 35 regressions and the mutually guarded cancellation schedule.
35/35 regressions passed; transitive rank checks rejected mutually guarded cancellation handlers while active-resumption borrows remained valid.
ContinuationSafe v0.6 extends v0.5’s cleanup-rank inference to transitive cancellation-handler captures, rejecting mutually guarded cancellation.
Mechanize ContinuationSafe v0.6 preservation and cleanup proofs, checking guard drainage after finite resumptions and exactly-once finalization under cancellation.
ContinuationSafe v0.6 mechanization proves preservation and, after handler closure and finite resumptions, guard drainage and exactly-once finalization under cancellation.
Model-check ContinuationSafe v0.6 under reentrant cancellation (≤4 owners, ≤3 resumptions), checking rank compliance, borrow validity, and cleanup.
Across ≤4 owners and ≤3 resumptions, rank-compliant schedules showed zero deadlocks or dangling borrows; terminal owners finalized once.
Adopt v0.6’s cleanup ranks for finalizers and cancellation handlers: 35/35 tests pass, and finite-resumption cleanup is proved.
